findings.obligation: L1/F101: a resuming run keeps as read exactly the rows of the plan it resumes that were already read; and the oracle rule that an expected or observed value is taken from the contract, never fabricated by the test, so that RED names missing production behaviour rather than the test's own literal.
findings.observation: The binding sets carries_an_earlier_read to the literal false for every kept row, so carried_reads() is the empty set independently of what resume_plan answers. Measured: left {} right {1} on the minimal plan [StillToRead, AlreadyRead]; the generator guarantees an AlreadyRead row, so the assertion fails for every input and no production change can turn it green while these bytes stand. The crafter may not edit the oracle, so this obligation has no reachable GREEN. Worse, when the design's declared answers land (Resume::kept -> Vec<KeptRow> and record_plan over ScanPlanRow), the closure |position| KeptRepo { position, .. } stops type-checking and the whole target fails to build, taking the genuinely RED journey L5/F120 down with it into BROKEN.
findings.remediation: Remove the fabricated flag. Either (a) bind L1 to the design's declared answer (KeptRow.status == PlanRowStatus::Read) and move the two not-yet-buildable observations into their own test target so the journey's semantic RED stays observable today, or (b) observe the same law through a surface this design leaves unchanged - the resuming run's frozen plan read back with ScanPlanRead::latest_plan, whose rows already carry PlanRowStatus - so the binding needs no edit when craft lands. Either way no mapping may remain that the crafter would have to change.

findings.obligation: L4/F115: a plan written with its row statuses reads back with the same repos, the same order and the same statuses.
findings.observation: The binding maps StoredRepo to PlannedScanRepo and drops the status before calling store.record_plan(OWNER, run, &repos), today's signature at crates/ports/src/review.rs:457. The status therefore never reaches the writer under test: the measured failure (all three rows read back StillToRead against an expected first AlreadyRead) observes the oracle deleting the status, not the adapter refusing to keep it. The round trip has no falsifier for the declared writer, and once record_plan takes &[ScanPlanRow] this call no longer compiles, which the crafter may not fix.
findings.remediation: Build ports::ScanPlanRow values (the type already exists at crates/ports/src/review.rs:555) and pass them to the declared record_plan, so the only thing missing is the production signature and the failure names it; keep that observation in a target whose build state cannot mask the journey's RED. If the round trip cannot be expressed before craft, state it as an uncovered obligation instead of an assertion that observes the test's own deletion.

findings.obligation: L2/F107 covering promise P2: a row a resume takes over as read is never among the rows it reads now, so a repo is counted once.
findings.observation: Because the same binding leaves carries_an_earlier_read false everywhere, the carried set is always empty and its intersection with reads_now is empty for every production behaviour. The test passed in the measured run, but it passes for free: it cannot fail, so it is not yet a falsifier for P2 and its reported green carries no information about the promise.
findings.remediation: After the binding is corrected, confirm this property goes red on the wrong behaviour it names (a run that carries every kept row as already read, N2) before relying on its green.

L5/F120, the journey, is genuine semantic RED at the public driving port. Printed evidence: her paused run read priyaraman/tidepool, the run she picked up read priyaraman/kelp and priyaraman/quill-docs, her stored run status is completed, and her queue status region reads verbatim '2 repos read'. Assertion: left 2, right 3. The stimulus reaches the queue page through the real binary over HTTP, the observation is the rendered line, and the falsifier named in the design (two repos read, more than three, or no line at all) is the one the assertion discriminates. This failure is the missing production behaviour, not scaffolding.

Production today is Resume { to_read, carried, skipped } with kept() -> Vec<usize> (crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/resume.rs:91-100), so no production change makes this assertion pass while these oracle bytes stand.

diagnostic: Rejected: two of the eight declared S1 observations have no falsifier over production. The journey L5/F120 is sound and is genuine semantic RED at the public HTTP port ('2 repos read' against three repos read across the pause), and L3/F111, L4/F116, L4/F117 and T1 are sound; but L1/F101 and L4/F115 fail on values the oracle itself writes - a hardcoded carries_an_earlier_read: false at :181 and a status dropped before record_plan at :219 - so neither can ever go green while the crafter is forbidden to edit the oracle, and L2/F107's green is pass-for-free for the same reason. The flagged in-oracle sut_* bindings are the defect: not because they reach below the HTTP port (review-domain's and the store's public APIs are legitimate surfaces for these laws), but because they answer the assertion themselves instead of carrying production's answer, and because they will stop compiling the moment the declared Resume::kept and record_plan land, turning the whole target, journey included, into BROKEN at exactly the commit that should turn it green. Remediation is the oracle owner's: bind to the declared answers (KeptRow.status, ports::ScanPlanRow) or to a surface this design leaves unchanged (latest_plan's PlanRowStatus rows), keeping the journey's observable RED in a target that still builds.
